title: Staying with the Shaw grandparents in Montgomery before settling in Tuskegee
summary: The family lives with his mother's parents in Montgomery while she waits for a Tuskegee post, then settles in Greenwood; he recalls his grandfather and his parents' origins.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes, they'd left Texas to go to
Alabama, and my father got this job at Tuskegee Institute -- and Booker T. Washington was still President and founder of that school in Tuskegee.

But then my mother didn't have a job there, and until he could get her on the faculty there, she took me and my brother, Gus, and we lived a little while at my grandparents' home in Montgomery, Alabama, and went to the elementary school of Alabama State for awhile. And then later on, my father got my mother a job teaching elementary adult classes in Tuskegee, and then we all --she moved, and rejoined my father there in a house that was part of his job at that time, for the whole family. So we were residents of the residential community called Greenwood, outside of -- just on the edge of the campus.
So that was home and schooling, and my father and mother's job all in one -- and my brother and I went right on up through that school on through high school.
That's great. Now which grandparents were these, Teddy?
These are my mother's parents in Montgomery. I have no knowledge of my father's parents, except that --
What were their names, Teddy?
Shaw was that family name.
Uh huh. Your grandfather on your
mother's side was -- Shaw.
But do you remember his first name?

I don't know -- everybody used to just call him 'Grandpa Shaw' or Papa Shaw; I mean, we're going back to when I was only 5 or 6 years old. See, he died -- oh, I remember, at that time he was in his seventies, when I first saw him coming from Texas.

But I really can't remember his first name. But my grandfather was a preacher and a barber, I believe, was his work over the years, and he had a big family -- my mother came from a large family. There were six -- evenly divided -- six girls and six boys in the family, and they've all passed on now in 1979, except for three of the girls [who] are still alive. My mother has passed away, but the three youngest sisters are still alive, and the three older have died, and all six of the men in the family died.
Uh huh.
So you went through school in Montgomery -- is that right?

No. Just a short period of schooling in Montgomery -- between Texas and Tuskegee, until my father could arrange to get my mother on the staff of Tuskegee, teaching there, we lived at her parents' home in Montgomery, and temporarily went to the elementary school
at Alabama State, which had an elementary department in those days, with little kids.
Uh huh. And where did you go when you were in elementary and high school; I mean, what towns would you be in?

Well, that would be when I got to Tuskegee. So I got a little elementary schooling in Austin, Texas, and then a little in Montgomery -- and then by the time we got to Tuskegee, I think I entered officially the third grade, I believe it would be, in Tuskegee.
Uh huh, I see.

My brother and I were both in the third grade by the time my father got the whole family settled in Tuskegee which was to be, spend the remainder of his life and also my mother's life, in Tuskegee. Both of them are buried right on the campus -- in the graveyard on the campus of Tuskegee right now.
Uh huh.
So they spent the rest of their lives at Tuskegee, from those days.
Did your mother ever teach in Tennessee?
No -- but my mother was born in Tennessee.
Oh, I see.

I think she was born in either Cumberland, Tennessee or in Cumberland County or something like that. I never really tracked that down too much. But it was Tennessee. My father was born in Pennsylvania.
